A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SliceQuantiles research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 report original experiments on AdultAge and AdultHours, including maximum rank errors across 200 runs.

after.justification: Section 6 reports original experiments, supplemented by spacing calculations and additional empirical comparisons in Appendices D and E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes h from ceil(ell/2) to ceil((ell-1)/2), with revised boundary and strict nonoverlap conditions in Good. The correlated-noise slicing and per-slice median mechanism remain. Range clipping disappears from the pseudocode but remains described in Section 3.2, so it was not removed from the supported method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate multiple-quantile estimation on AdultAge and AdultHours under substitute and add/remove adjacency. The added privacy budgets, replication factors, and histogram configurations vary settings within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds the Hist estimator from Lalanne, Garivier, and Gribonval, evaluated with N/10, N/2, and N bins in Figure 4. AQ with approximate and pure privacy accounting remains. AppindExp is discussed as excluded, not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes stated data replication from 10 to 12 and sampled quantiles per run from 200 to m. Appendix E adds ε=0.5 and ε=5, using 1,172,208 and 293,052 points respectively; ε=1 uses 586,104 points. These materially revise and extend the reported settings, without establishing which revisions reflect reruns rather than corrections.

E4.justification: V2 adds required-spacing sensitivity to δ and its slice/counting decomposition in Figure 2, processed-data distribution analyses in Figure 3, and privacy-budget/sample-size and histogram-bin sensitivity comparisons in Figure 4. These extend v1's number-of-quantiles sweep to additional questions about applicability and parameter sensitivity.

E5.justification: Both versions report 200 runs and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. V2 explicitly connects bootstrapping to those 200 experiments, but introduces no different run count, seed reporting, or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figure 1 contains replaced numerical curves under revised reported settings, while retaining the broad advantage of SliceQuantiles. Figures 2–4 add spacing calculations, distribution results, and Hist/additional-budget scores. Hist has substantially larger errors in the reported comparisons. The changed dataset sizes prevent interpreting cross-version curves as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.1 becomes conditional on avoiding the failure branch. Corollaries 5.2–5.3 revise slice sizes, gap requirements, and success probabilities from 1−4β and 1−3β to 1−β−γ and 1−β−δ. V2 also corrects Definition 2.1 and Appendix B.2, reworks Theorem C.1, and adds the Chernoff-bound derivation in Appendix D. The headline asymptotic error rates remain.

C1.justification: The principal privacy and error-reduction contributions remain. Section 1.1 adds an explicit gap-free guarantee obtained by merging quantiles, with error O((log b + log m log(m/δ))/ε), and qualifies the improvement-factor comparison by b≥m. V1 discussed merging only under the narrower condition in Section 5.2.

C2.justification: The limitations discussion now emphasizes practical summary quantiles and a reported required gap below 0.005. V2 also explains Hist's errors through distribution approximation and bin choice. The warning that competing methods can win for extremely large domains is retained in Section 1.1 rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix D replaces v1's generic reference to tail bounds with an explicit calibration procedure: discrete-Laplace moment generating functions, Chernoff and union bounds, and a 100-point search over λ. Appendix E supplies histogram configurations and exact augmented sample counts. This substantially improves implementation documentation; the code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and discussion concerning absolute-error estimation, streaming, local/distributed privacy, and discrete-Laplace analysis, while dropping the McSherry–Talwar reference. Section 1.1 distinguishes these alternative formulations from rank-error quantiles. The central positioning against Kaplan et al. and threshold-learning methods remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and overall argument are retained. V2 refines terminology and selected explanations, rewrites the limitations and experimental descriptions, and separates optional clipping from the base algorithm presentation. Appendices D and E extend the existing structure.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1 with revised axis and legend styling and a clarified privacy caption. It adds the spacing-decomposition plot, paired distribution plots, and twelve-panel comparison in Figures 2–4. Algorithm 1 is also simplified visually, while Table 1 retains its structure.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through explicit spacing calibration and strengthens empirical support with Hist and additional privacy budgets. It also fixes identifiable errors in the privacy definition and substitution-proof calculation. The gain is qualified: budget comparisons also change sample size, and the revised utility success probabilities are not fully reconciled with the retained proof in Appendix C.1.
